C-WIN-ROLLBACK-PANIC.Summary: Restore the Windows Help-menu rollback: mt_rollback_restore currently panics on Windows before the first network response because ReqwestFetch::get builds a fresh current-thread tokio runtime and calls Runtime::block_on inside Tauri's async command task (pinned tokio 1.54.1 documents the panic; pinned tauri 2.12.5 runs async commands on its tokio async_runtime), so the renderer's invoke never settles and a confirmed rollback silently aborts. This bundle moves the blocking verified-restore execution off the async task (the mt_rollback_prepare spawn_blocking precedent, or the established non-async rollback CLI machinery re-used by the menu off the async context), gives both Windows rollback fetches and the overall operation an explicit deadline, and persists the pending-installer fact so the pending window is accounted across the restoring process's exit — on both desktop platforms the menu rollback either completes or surfaces the localized honest error.
C-WIN-ROLLBACK-PANIC.Problem: With a valid rollback set, the Windows menu rollback aborts before any network traffic. mt_rollback_restore (src-tauri/src/m068_rollback.rs:1971-1975) is an async #[tauri::command]; Tauri 2.12.5 (Cargo.lock:4901-4903) executes async command handlers on its Tokio-based async_runtime. Its non-macOS branch (:2005-2027) calls restore_inner, which on Windows fetches through ReqwestFetch::get (:956-971): that builds a new current-thread tokio Runtime and calls rt.block_on(...) — and tokio 1.54.1 (Cargo.lock:5433-5435) panics when Runtime::block_on is entered from within another runtime's context. The command task dies mid-flight; the renderer's CONFIRM_ROLLBACK await of invoke('mt_rollback_restore') (src/renderer/src/store/autoUpdates.js:406-430) never resolves and never rejects, so even the localized rollback.restoreFailedTitle/Body error notice added by C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES is unreachable on this path. The user's confirmed rollback silently interrupts; the snapshot survives and recovery degenerates to the manual pre-boot mark --rollback run or a release-history download (integration-reliability audit 2026-11-20, F-001, high). Two same-file gaps keep the menu path from honestly completing even once the panic is removed. First (F-007): both Windows restore fetches — the release's latest.json and the installer bytes (restore_windows_flow, m068_rollback.rs:1535-1566) — run on reqwest 0.13.5 (Cargo.lock:4016-4018) defaults with no overall deadline, so a stalled transfer wedges the restore and holds the instance lock until the process is killed; the CLI repeats blindly because the second command cannot acquire the lock. Second (F-006): nothing persists the pending-installer state — after mt_rollback_restore spawns the verified installer and exits (:2014-2027), the next launch only version-compares in finalize_finished_restore (:828-843), so a rollback re-run inside the pending window can spawn a second installer for the same release; R-3's pending-window serialization ("a staging-area lock or marker ... so a second headless run cannot re-spawn the installer") was never implemented and was explicitly deferred to a follow-up by C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES. macOS is unaffected by the panic (its GUI branch runs gui_restore_core, no fetch), but the bar this bundle sets applies to both platforms: the menu rollback completes or surfaces an honest error.
C-WIN-ROLLBACK-PANIC.Relationship: Lineage: C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK introduced restore_inner, ReqwestFetch and R-3's pending-window serialization requirement; C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES factored the host-agnostic restore_windows_flow with its injected stage/verify seams and recorded the never-implemented pending-window marker in its DeferredDecisions as the rollback-integrity follow-up this bundle discharges; C-ROLLBACK-STORE-BUILD-GUARD aligned the desktop-only cfg guards this fix preserves; C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES added the renderer honest-error notice (rollback.restoreFailedTitle/Body, source rollback) that this bundle makes reachable by turning panics and stalls into real command rejections. Source: integration-reliability audit 2026-11-20 (main 35c922373514ea677fda2f537220b36865a1e785), remediation group "Восстановить путь отката из меню Windows" bundling F-001 (high) with F-006 and F-007 (medium); this spec mirrors that group's three-item checklist in its AcceptanceCriteria. Same-run adjacency, read-only: F-004 (no check/install deadlines in the forward updater, src-tauri/src/m016_updater.rs:61-76) belongs to the separate updater remediation group (F-003/F-004/F-005) and is not fixed here; this bundle's deadline covers only the rollback transport (ReqwestFetch and restore_windows_flow), never tauri-plugin-updater, and M-016's status-check contract is untouched. F-008 (re-install overlaps snapshot preparation) is cut from this bundle — justification in Constraints and NonGoals.

Goals.R-1: Panic removal (F-001): no rollback restore may start a tokio runtime inside Tauri's async task. The synchronous verified restore — restore_inner with its Windows branch, and the macOS gui_restore_core sibling — executes off the async context: the established mt_rollback_prepare pattern (tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking) wrapping the existing synchronous core, or equivalently the established non-async rollback CLI machinery re-used by the menu off the async context; the exact mechanism is fixed at plan time. Unit-level contract: the block_on site is unreachable from the async command context on every platform, and the Fetch trait keeps its synchronous shape and injected test seams. The macOS branch's app.restart() and the Windows branch's app.exit(0) stay on the async side after the blocking work joins.
Goals.R-2: Network deadline (F-007): both Windows restore fetches (latest.json feed + installer) and the restore operation as a whole carry explicit deadlines; a stalled or non-progressing transfer ends the restore with the controlled exit-4-class failure on the CLI path and a String error on the menu path, leaves the rollback set untouched (no mutation has happened — verification and staging strictly precede the writes, unchanged), and releases the instance lock / returns the renderer to its terminal state. No silent unbounded wait remains on any rollback network path. The deadline enters ReqwestFetch's client builder (or a wrapper), not the Fetch trait; the happy path still performs exactly two GETs on Windows and zero on macOS.
Goals.R-3: Installer accounting (F-006): before spawning the verified installer, the restore persists a pending-rollback fact at the rollback root (target version, write timestamp, a marker of the pre-operation state). The boot reconciliation table distinguishes three states at the next launch: (a) the version transition confirmed (running version equals the manifest's previous version — finalize and clear, existing behavior preserved); (b) the pending installer still running — a rollback retry declines without spawning a second installer for the same release; (c) the pending installer failed or is gone — the pending fact clears and an idempotent retry is available. The lifetime instance lock keeps serializing live processes exactly as today; the persisted fact's only job is to bridge the pending window across the restoring process's exit, which the lock cannot cover. Exact mechanism (child-pid liveness with a timestamp bound, a completion handshake, or equivalent) is fixed at plan time and must fail toward "retry allowed" only on positive confirmation of failure — a false "failed" verdict would spawn the second installer this goal exists to prevent.
Goals.R-4: Honest menu outcome, both platforms: from the Help-menu confirmation on macOS and Windows the rollback ends in exactly one terminal renderer state — success (Windows: the app hands off to the spawned installer and exits; macOS: relaunch into the restored version) or the localized rollback.restoreFailed* error notice driven by a real command rejection — never a silently unresolved invoke, never a panic reaching the user. Raw errors stay console-only per the C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES voice; if the renderer needs a bounded-wait guard so a wedged command can no longer strand the UI silently, its mechanism is fixed at plan time.
Goals.R-5: No regression: macOS menu rollback behavior, the CLI --rollback surface and its exit-code table, the verification order fetch→verify→stage→prefs→re-digest→spawn, deterministic asset derivation, strict manifest validation, the four inert app-store stubs, and the C-ROLLBACK-STORE-BUILD-GUARD desktop-only cfg alignment are all preserved; existing suites keep passing with their bodies unchanged in meaning.

Constraints.Constraint: ObservedWriteScope: src-tauri/src/m068_rollback.rs plus its inline test modules (rollback_core, rollback_restore, rollback_cli, rollback_windows_flow, rollback_boot, rollback_restore_outcome, rollback_store_stubs, and the macOS-gated rollback_swap, rollback_gui_restore, rollback_norelaunch); src/renderer/src/store/autoUpdates.js limited to the CONFIRM_ROLLBACK error-surfacing block (:406-430) and its pins in tests/renderer/store/autoUpdates.test.js; and the GRACE graph/verification anchors — .grace/graph/features.xml M-068 (Summary/SummaryDelta), .grace/graph/runtime.xml M-068, .grace/verification/features.xml V-M-068. No changes to src-tauri/src/m016_updater.rs, src-tauri/tauri.conf.json, src-tauri/src/main.rs command registration, Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock (a reqwest client-builder timeout is a setting, not a dependency change), prepare_inner, installSignedUpdate, or locale keys beyond reusing the existing rollback feedback strings.

Fix direction is binding: the blocking fetch leaves the async task (spawn_blocking per the mt_rollback_prepare precedent, or the established non-async rollback CLI path re-used by the menu off the async context). The synchronous Fetch trait and its injected test seams survive unchanged; the deadline lands in the production transport only (ReqwestFetch builder), keeping tests network-free.

Both-platforms bar: the menu path must complete or surface an honest error on BOTH macOS and Windows; macOS behavior is otherwise unchanged. The panic is Windows-only; the deadline and accounting work is exercised through the host-agnostic seams on the reference macOS host, with the true Windows proof riding the owner manual protocol (VerificationIntent).

Bundle cut, by file-sharing and risk: F-007 is IN — it shares m068_rollback.rs and the exact transport seam the panic fix must touch (ReqwestFetch + restore_windows_flow), and without a deadline the fixed menu path still fails the R-4 bar (a stalled transfer is a silent hang, the same defect class as the panic); the change is a client-builder setting plus typed error mapping, low incremental risk, unit-testable through existing injected seams. F-006 is IN — all its evidence sites live in m068_rollback.rs (:828-843 finalize, :1574-1617 flow, :1830-1845 lock, :1908-1938 spawn refs), its pending-window serialization is the requirement C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES explicitly deferred to this follow-up, and its state file plus reconcile branches extend the module's existing boot decision table; moderate risk is bounded by R-3's fail-toward-retry-only-on-confirmed-failure rule. F-008 is OUT — its mechanism spans renderer install entry points (prefComponents/tabs/general/index.vue button gating, commands/index.js installSignedUpdate with no in-flight guard) and the forward-update prepare staging lifecycle (prepare_inner, m068_rollback.rs:406-432), none of which the panic/deadline/accounting fixes modify; the audit assigns it its own remediation group ("Допускать одну установку обновления на профиль"); bundling it would widen the write scope into M-016-adjacent renderer surfaces with no shared mechanism. F-004 stays a read-only reference (separate updater group, see Relationship).

Verification and trust ordering untouched: minisign verification against the pinned pubkey, feed-version agreement, deterministic asset derivation, snapshot strict validation, and the write ordering all keep their current contracts; this bundle adds no fetch surface, no telemetry, and no new network calls beyond the existing two.

Gates: existing rollback suites, renderer updater/autoUpdates/rollbackConfirm suites and i18n coverage stay green; grace lint delta clean against the recorded pre-existing baseline (current before editing, --change FIX-WIN-ROLLBACK-PANIC target during, final --run-commands before handoff); app-store builds keep no rollback surface anywhere.

No version change, release, tag or publication is authorized by this specification. Spec-only pass: implementation belongs to the approved plan; this draft enters the repo under .grace/changes/ through the standard review gates (two consecutive clean four-corner passes recorded before owner approval is requested).

NonGoals.NonGoal: F-008 per-profile install ownership across the forward-update surfaces (settings button, notice, notification, installSignedUpdate) — a separate change with its own renderer scope.

Forward updater deadlines, independent GitHub download or source-failover behavior (F-003/F-004/F-005 group): m016_updater.rs, tauri.conf.json, tauri-plugin-updater and the release pipeline are untouched.

Making ReqwestFetch async, reworking the Fetch trait, or any transport redesign beyond thread placement and a deadline; changing the minisign trust anchor, asset naming, feed endpoints or the stats gateway.

The GUI-side lockless start when a headless restore holds the instance lock (C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES DeferredDecisions) — a separate follow-up; R-3's accounting is the persisted pending-installer fact, not the live instance lock.

Multi-version rollback history, automatic crash-loop detection, auto-rollback, and Windows assets for releases published without the WINDOWS_RELEASE variable (the documented release-history fallback stays the answer).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Menu rollback completes on Windows (owner-run clean-VM protocol, the audit's checklist item 1): with a valid rollback set, the Help-menu rollback reaches the installer fixture without a panic; the renderer lands in the success handoff state and the machine-readable outcome stays truthful.

Stalled transfer ends in a controlled error (checklist item 2): with the network fixture stalled past the deadline, both the menu and CLI paths terminate with the typed deadline failure, the rollback set is intact, the instance lock no longer blocks a fresh probe, and the renderer shows the localized rollback.restoreFailed* notice — never a hang, never a second silent interruption.

Pending-window accounting (checklist item 3): a rollback re-run while the spawned installer is still running launches no second installer and reports the pending state; after a confirmed installer failure the next launch clears the pending fact and an idempotent retry is available; a confirmed version transition still finalizes and clears exactly as today.

Unit-level — panic site unreachable: a test pins that the async command dispatches the restore core through spawn_blocking (or the equivalent off-async mechanism) on every platform, so Runtime::block_on never runs inside a runtime context; every existing restore_windows_flow failure-path test keeps driving the same flow on the reference macOS host.

Unit-level — network deadline: an injected non-progressing fetch fixture ends the restore with the deadline error before any mutation; the fetch-count contract (exactly two GETs on the Windows happy path, zero on macOS) is pinned unchanged.

Unit-level — install accounting: the pending fact is written before the spawn, the boot reconciliation distinguishes running/succeeded/failed in all three branches, and the accounting never blocks or delays the confirmed-success finalize.

Renderer: autoUpdates.test.js keeps the C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES honest-error pins green (a real rejection raises the localized notice, the card stays hidden, zero unhandled rejections) and, if a bounded-wait guard lands, pins that its expiry surfaces the same notice; rollbackConfirm.test.js hygiene pins unchanged.

Governance: M-068 and V-M-068 deltas land in the same bundle as the code (living-tracker evidence naming the new tests); app-store stub suite unchanged and green; no version bump; grace lint final clean with commands run.

AffectedAreas.Item: .grace/graph/features.xml (M-068 Summary/SummaryDelta), .grace/graph/runtime.xml (M-068 entry), .grace/verification/features.xml (V-M-068 scenarios/evidence) — updated in the implementation bundle, strictly on the M-068/V-M-068 entries, no other change's entry touched.
M-016 adjacency is read-only: mt_updater_check and installSignedUpdate contracts are untouched; the rollback deadline does not extend to tauri-plugin-updater.

Renderer evidence: the honest-error pins of the C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES suites stay green with any bounded-wait addition pinned to the same localized copy. Two-platform manual protocol debt: V-M-068 already records the owner-discharged protocol (a real two-version menu restore on macOS and a polygon/laptop-kari Windows restore through the verified installer, transcript carrying every BLOCK_ROLLBACK_* marker and exactly one MARK_ROLLBACK line) — this bundle's Windows menu-rollback-in-a-clean-VM acceptance rides and extends that protocol and is discharged by the owner with an attached transcript; unit tests do not auto-discharge it. grace lint --path . --change FIX-WIN-ROLLBACK-PANIC --assertions target during implementation and --assertions final --run-commands before handoff, with the pre-change current-state lint recorded as the baseline.
